annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: I keep trying to picture what he'd ask of me, and I just can't
annotations.pd_decision_conflict: So I'd rather not choose. I really would rather not.

annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: what that worker would expect from a stranger at the station, and I come up blank
annotations.pd_decision_conflict: I don't want to answer this.

annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: Would he forgive a stranger who pulled that lever? I genuinely can't work that out
annotations.pda_responsibility: Pulling the lever makes it my doing, and leaving it makes it my doing too
annotations.pd_decision_conflict: wishing it were anyone's hand but mine

annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: how does the worker on the side track see being one person weighed against five? I can't read that
annotations.pd_decision_conflict: I think the numbers would win in the end, and I'd hate that they did.

annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: trying to figure out what the five on the main line would want from me
annotations.pda_responsibility: freezing counts as a choice too

annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: I can't tell what the man alone on that siding would expect
imagine what the person on the side track would say... my imagination just stops
I can't work out what any of the five would think of being saved that way
When I try to guess what the side-track worker would wish for, I hit a wall
annotations.pd_decision_conflict: It feels like both paths end somewhere dark.

annotations.ce_mentalizing_difficulty: I can't figure out what the lone worker would want from me
annotations.pd_decision_conflict: I'm worn out just thinking about it
